Low carbohydrate intake shifts the body toward fat oxidation and ketone production (ketosis), and it raises gluconeogenesis from amino acids and glycerol to keep blood glucose up. The team note's claim that muscles speed up glycogen breakdown to compensate is not right. Muscle glycogen stores run down, and muscle can't release glucose into the blood because it lacks glucose-6-phosphatase. Your question looks cut off, so if it's multiple choice, send me the options.
